verses.text: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam became king of Judah.
He ruled in Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
He followed all the sinful ways of his father before him. His heart wasn't fully devoted to the LORD his God as the heart of his ancestor David had been.
Still, for David's sake the LORD his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem by raising up his son to succeed him and keeping Jerusalem secure.
David had done what was right in the LORD's eyes and had followed everything the LORD commanded all his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
Rehoboam and Jeroboam were at war all through Rehoboam's life.
The rest of Abijam's acts and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah. Abijam and Jeroboam were at war.
Abijam died and joined his ancestors. They buried him in David's City, and his son Asa became king in his place.
In the twentieth year of King Jeroboam's reign over Israel, Asa became king of Judah.
He ruled in Jerusalem for forty-one years. His mother was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
Asa did what was right in the LORD's eyes, as his ancestor David had done.
He drove the male shrine prostitutes out of the land and removed all the idols his ancestors had made.
He removed his mother Maacah from her position as queen mother because she had made a detestable image for Asherah. Asa cut it down and burned it by the Kidron stream.
The high places remained, though Asa was fully devoted to the LORD all his life.
He brought the silver, gold, and utensils that he and his father had dedicated into the LORD's house.
Asa and King Baasha of Israel were at war throughout their reigns.
King Baasha of Israel moved against Judah and fortified Ramah to block anyone from coming or going from the territory of Asa king of Judah.

Asa took all the silver and gold left in the treasuries of the LORD's house and the palace and handed it to his servants. King Asa sent them to Ben Hadad son of Tabrimmon and grandson of Hezion, the king of Syria, who lived in Damascus. He sent this message:
“Let's make a treaty like the one our fathers made. I'm sending you silver and gold as a gift. Break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel so he'll withdraw from my land.”
Ben Hadad listened to King Asa and sent his army commanders against Israel's towns. They struck Ijon, Dan, Abel Beth Maacah, all Chinneroth, and the whole land of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard what had happened, he stopped building Ramah and stayed in Tirzah.
King Asa issued an order to all Judah, with no exceptions. They carried away the stone and timber Baasha had used to build Ramah. King Asa used it to build up Geba in Benjamin and Mizpah.
The rest of Asa's acts, his strength, all he did, and the towns he built are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah. In his old age he developed a disease in his feet.
Asa died and joined his ancestors. He was buried with them in the city of his ancestor David, and his son Jehoshaphat became king in his place.
Jeroboam's son Nadab became king of Israel in the second year of King Asa's reign over Judah, and he ruled Israel for two years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's sight, following his father's ways and repeating the sin his father had led Israel into.
Baasha son of Ahijah, from the tribe of Issachar, plotted against Nadab. As Nadab and all Israel were besieging the Philistine town of Gibbethon, Baasha struck him down there.
Baasha killed Nadab in the third year of King Asa's reign over Judah and became king in Nadab's place.
As soon as Baasha became king, he struck down Jeroboam's entire family. He left no one in the family alive, just as the LORD had said through his servant Ahijah from Shiloh.
This happened because Jeroboam had sinned and led Israel into sin, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger.
The rest of Nadab's acts and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Asa and King Baasha of Israel were at war throughout their reigns.
In the third year of King Asa's reign over Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel. He ruled in Tirzah for twenty-four years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's sight. He followed Jeroboam's ways and repeated the sin Jeroboam had led Israel into.
